records.title: Would Android drive a standard HID haptic pen?
records.summary: No Android API was found that sends HID Haptics page (0x0E) commands to a stylus. Whether Linux or Android route them at all is unknown.
details: If they did, a pen built to the Windows guide could work on Android without a vendor service.
Next step: check AOSP inputflinger and the Linux HID subsystem for Haptics page support.

records.title: Huawei M-Pencil Pro haptic API
records.summary: Huawei's public developer documentation has not shown a direct M-Pencil Pro haptic API.
details: Useful mainly for studying another system-managed feedback design.

records.title: Lenovo LPP haptic command interface
records.summary: No public Android SDK or community implementation found for AP600U haptics.
details: Treat LPP as a research target, not an established standard.
Possible lead: LPP code in Lenovo system packages or firmware source releases.

records.title: Unexplained parts of the OnePlus interface
records.summary: Several calls and values are declared but their meaning has not been confirmed.
details: getSupportFeatureList(): no transaction code in the reconstruction.
startVibration(int): what values it takes, and whether it plays a one-off pulse.
FUNCTION_VIBRATION (4) and IpeFeature: where each is used.
getPencilConnectState(): what the integer states mean.
Demo mode: what enableDemoMode changes.

records.title: How does an app join OnePlus's approved pen SDK?
records.summary: The supported route for third-party apps exists, but its availability, application process and terms are unknown.
details: Known: approved apps such as HiPaint authenticate with OnePlus through a developer SDK.
Unknown: whether the SDK is public, how to apply, what it checks and what it costs.
Next step: ask OnePlus developer relations or HiPaint's developer.

records.title: What does the service send to the pen, and when?
records.summary: It is not known whether a haptic session is one start command with the pen playing on contact, or a stream of commands during writing.
details: The interface shape (set type, start, stop) and the Windows model both suggest the pen plays the texture locally on contact.
Next step: an HCI snoop log of a writing session in OnePlus Notes would show the pattern.
records.basis: Open question from the research order.

records.title: Which firmware directory does each tablet need?
records.summary: Partly answered: the directory is named after the tablet's ro.boot.prjname. Still unknown: which number in each pair is Chinese and which global, and what the converted Pad 3 reports.
details: Answered: jjhitel's fix creates /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/<ro.boot.prjname>/, and users report it restores the pen.
Known numbers: 23926, 23927, 23976, 23978 (Pad Pro / Pad 2); 24926, 24976 (Pad 2 Pro family).

On the Pad 3: run getprop ro.boot.prjname and ls -lR /odm/firmware/wireless_pen/, hash each cps8601_firmware.bin, and check dmesg | grep cps8601 after attaching the pen. The commands are listed in research/docs/pen-attach-handshake.md.
Also unknown: how 24976's firmware compares with 24926's, and whether KernelSU mounts a module's top-level odm/ folder.
To settle how the driver builds the path, read the GPL source of oplus_wireless_pen in OnePlus's kernel release.
records.basis: Open question from the 2 Nov 2026 firmware review.

records.title: Advertised versus delivered pressure
records.summary: Advertised figures such as 16,000 or 16,384 levels may not match what apps receive on a given pen and tablet.
details: Next step: read InputDevice.getMotionRange(AXIS_PRESSURE) and getevent -lp on the Pad 3 with the Stylo 2.

records.title: Does USI define haptics?
records.summary: Public USI 2.0 coverage mentions no haptics, and the full spec is members-only.

records.title: Does Pencil Engine control the Focus Pen Pro motor?
records.summary: The published API list covers input and gestures. It does not show a haptic output call.
details: Don't mistake gesture support for haptic output control.
Next step: inspect the AAR once developer access is granted.
